candidate_sentences.text: LHV Group’s Q2 2026 net profit was EUR 24.7 million, up 25% from EUR 19.7 million in Q1 but down 20% from EUR 30.8 million in Q2 2025.
Return on equity improved to 13.1% from 10.7% in Q1 but remained below 17.4% a year earlier.

verified_key_information_units.information: Loan portfolio grew to EUR 5,768 million (+3% QoQ, +15% YoY) while deposits decreased by EUR 245 million QoQ (ordinary client deposits +EUR 105 million, financial intermediaries -EUR 74 million, platform deposits -EUR 276 million).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial Summary and Note 12: Loan portfolio growth, deposit breakdown by client type, and quarterly changes.

candidate_sentences.text: The Group’s loan portfolio grew 3% quarter-on-quarter and 15% year-on-year to EUR 5.8 billion, while customer deposits fell 3% from Q1 to EUR 7.6 billion, mainly because of reduced platform and financial-intermediary deposits.

verified_key_information_units.information: Subsidiary Q2 net profits: LHV Pank EUR 24.3 million, LHV Bank Limited EUR 1.4 million, AS LHV Varahaldus EUR 0.4 million, AS LHV Kindlustus EUR 0.8 million (LHV Paytech reported a net loss of EUR 0.3 million).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Overviews of AS LHV Pank, LHV Bank Limited, AS LHV Varahaldus, and AS LHV Kindlustus sections.

candidate_sentences.text: LHV Pank generated EUR 24.3 million of quarterly profit, up 20% from Q1 but down 18% year-on-year.
LHV Bank’s profit rose to EUR 1.4 million, and LHV Kindlustus returned to a EUR 0.8 million profit from a Q1 loss, aided by fewer major losses and lower loss frequency.
LHV Varahaldus earned EUR 0.4 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic operational developments: migration of LHV Pank's core systems to Amazon Web Services cloud environment, receipt of MiCA crypto-asset service provider licence, and planned rebranding to LHV Bank AS to support international growth.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Overview of AS LHV Pank section: details on cloud migration, MiCA licence, and name change plans.

candidate_sentences.text: The quarter also included strategic changes at LHV Pank, including migration of core systems to Amazon Web Services, adoption of product-based management, and receipt of Estonia’s first bank licence for regulated crypto-asset services under MiCA.

verified_key_information_units.information: Capital adequacy ratio of 20.8% (vs 22.4% at end-2025) and liquidity coverage ratio of 171.5% (vs 185.0% at end-2025), with core Tier 1 ratio at 15.81% and Tier 1 ratio at 17.49%.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: The Group's Liquidity, Capitalisation and Asset Quality section and Note 16.

candidate_sentences.text: Capital adequacy was 20.8%, down from 23.0% year-on-year, as risk-weighted assets increased.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operating environment impacted by Middle East conflict de-escalation and energy price volatility, with OECD forecasting 2.8% global growth for 2026 contingent on Strait of Hormuz stability.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Operating Environment section: geopolitical tensions, energy prices, and OECD economic outlook.

verified_key_information_units.information: First half 2026 consolidated results: net profit EUR 44.4 million (-26% YoY), net income EUR 152.7 million (approximately flat YoY), and loan impairment charges EUR 7.1 million (vs EUR 1.5 million in H1 2025).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial Summary tables for 6M 2026: net profit, net income, and impairment charges compared to 6M 2025.

candidate_sentences.text: First-half net profit reached EUR 44.4 million, 26% below the EUR 59.9 million reported for the first half of 2025.

verified_key_information_units.information: Loan and bond portfolio impairment charges increased to EUR 5.8 million in Q2 2026 (from EUR 1.3 million in Q1 2026 and EUR -4.2 million in Q2 2025), driven by model-based forward-looking provisions.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial Summary and Note 20: impairment charges for Q2 2026 and comparisons with prior periods.

candidate_sentences.text: Loan and bond portfolio losses were EUR 5.8 million in Q2, compared with EUR 1.3 million in Q1 and a EUR 4.2 million gain in Q2 2025.

Management said the charges reflected forward-looking model provisions and a limited number of specific client cases, while overall loan portfolio quality remained strong and some losses were not expected to materialize.

verified_key_information_units.information: Managed funds increased to EUR 1,790 million (+4% QoQ, +15% YoY) with LHV Varahaldus reporting strong Q2 performance in index funds, while actively managed pension funds showed mixed results.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Overview of AS LHV Varahaldus section: fund volumes, active clients, and performance of pension funds.

verified_key_information_units.information: Performance against financial plan: Q2 net income slightly below plan due to higher expenses, loan portfolio growth according to plan, but deposits remained below plan.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial Summary section: Management Board commentary on plan variances.

details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers the core material meaning of K1 (Q2 2026 headline financial performance), K2 (loan portfolio and deposits), K3 (subsidiary Q2 net profits), K4 (strategic operational developments), K5 (capital adequacy ratios), K7 (first half 2026 consolidated results), and K8 (loan and bond portfolio impairment charges). However, it omits the core material meaning of K6 (operating environment context), K9 (managed funds performance), and K10 (performance against financial plan), resulting in important omissions that affect the overall completeness assessment. The score reflects that most material information is represented, but several important items are missing.

coherence_issues.description: S1 states net profit was EUR 24.7 million, up 25% from Q1 but down 20% from Q2 2025, while S5 states net income rose 7.3% quarter-on-quarter and 7% year-on-year to EUR 79.0 million. The terms 'net profit' and 'net income' are used interchangeably in financial contexts, but the figures presented (EUR 24.7 million vs EUR 79.0 million) are substantially different, creating a logical gap without clarification.

candidate_sentences.text: LHV Group’s Q2 2026 net profit was EUR 24.7 million, up 25% from EUR 19.7 million in Q1 but down 20% from EUR 30.8 million in Q2 2025.
Net income rose 7.3% quarter-on-quarter and 7% year-on-year to EUR 79.0 million, supported primarily by net interest income, which increased 5% from Q1 to EUR 62.5 million and 8% from Q2 2025.

details.coherence_justification: The summary is generally coherent with a logical flow of information about financial performance, profitability, and business developments. Most statements are consistent with each other and build upon prior information. The primary issue is the discrepancy between 'net profit' in S1 and 'net income' in S5, which are presented as different figures without explanation, creating a logical gap. There are no self-contradictions, and the organization is clear with each sentence contributing to an overall picture of the company's Q2 performance. Repetition is minimal, and there are no severe organizational problems.
